prompt.text:
Implement a sparse hex-cell automaton in `solution.rs` with no external crates. Expose `pub type Cell = (i32, i32)`, `pub fn decode_flips(input: &str) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeSet<Cell>, String>`, and `pub fn advance(cells: &std::collections::BTreeSet<Cell>, rounds: usize) -> std::collections::BTreeSet<Cell>`. Each nonblank input line is a path made from tokens `r`, `l`, `ur`, `ul`, `dr`, and `dl`, mapped respectively to axial deltas `(1,0)`, `(-1,0)`, `(1,-1)`, `(0,-1)`, `(0,1)`, and `(-1,1)`. Scan tokens left-to-right; any other or incomplete token makes the entire decode fail. Each path toggles its destination in the set. Empty or all-blank input yields an empty set. During one round, a present cell survives with one or two present neighbors; an absent cell is born with exactly two. Cells with no relevant neighbors disappear. `rounds == 0` must return a clone, and the input set must never be mutated. Do not include `main`.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
